Vanessa / Dylan — thanks for the ping. Quick answers and resources below: 

1) SOC 2 / DPA — what to send today:
- SOC 2 summary (redwood.share link): https://redwood.share/docs/soc2-summary.pdf (one-pager that covers scope and last audit date).
- Full SOC 2 report: available under NDA; if SummitAI needs it, ask them to share an NDA and we will route to security.
- DPA template: attached (DPA-template.docx). For POCs we typically use the standard DPA with minimal edits.

2) Procurement path guidance:
- Card for POC: common and fastest. If SummitAI confirms card ok, we can provision a sandbox and invoice for the POC month. No PO required for initial trial in most cases.
- PO for production / Dedicated: standard — we support net-30/45 PO terms once legal review is complete.
- Marketplace: Redwood is listed on CloudMarket as of Q1 2026; pricing can be matched but there are reconciliation steps (billing flows through marketplace, which can add delay). Marketplace is recommended if the customer requires that procurement path for compliance/approved vendor lists.

3) Pricing / discount policy:
- For a short POC (<=30 days) we can offer a one-time promotional credit up to 15% at AE discretion for deals < $100k ARR equivalent. For this account, I approve a 10% POC credit to make the card path smoother. Please include the credit in the trial invoice.

4) Security questionnaire blockers to flag to SummitAI: retention windows, subprocessor list, inbound network segmentation (for private deployments), and encryption key management (KMS/HSM). If they share a questionnaire we will triage and escalate any non-standard asks to Security.

Next steps I recommend we send to SummitAI (Vanessa to send):
- SOC 2 summary link and DPA-template.docx (attached).
- Short note explaining card vs PO vs marketplace tradeoffs.
- Proposed POC invoice with 10% credit if they accept card payment.

I attached the DPA-template.docx to this reply. Happy to jump on a quick call if they have legal questions.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
